title: Request Context Assembler for LLM KPI Enrichment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, pluggable Request Context Assembler (RCA) that attaches consistent, low-cardinality context to per-request metrics and spans for inference (latency, token count, kv-cache hit/miss), and emits both Prometheus-friendly metrics and OTLP envelopes suitable for downstream KPI pipelines.

Motivation: Current ingestion paths miss normalized request context (customer_id aliasing, model_variant, route_id, kv_cache_state) causing noisy cardinality and broken rollups in per-route latency dashboards. RCA will centralize enrichment in the edge/ingest layer, provide deterministic label canonicalization, and expose controlled sampling hooks for traces.

Design principles:
- Minimal latency addition: RCA must add <200us p50 to the request path in edge probes. Critical codepath is hot; implement in Rust/Golang sidecar with efficient zero-copy label mapping.
- Cardinality guardrails: Support configured allowlists and TTL-based canonicalization for dynamic labels (prompt_hash, session_id). All high-cardinality keys must be hashed/tagged and routed to separate ephemeral facets.
- Dual output: produce both Prometheus-style metric samples (for short-window dashboards) and OTLP metrics/spans with enriched attributes for long-term KPI computation. Mapping rules documented in Confluence doc.
- Tracing hooks: integrate with existing tracing agent to attach request_id, bucketed-token-count, kv-cache-hit boolean, and model_version to spans. Provide a sampling decision API that telemetry fabric can override.
- Backpressure & resilience: if downstream metric gateway is unavailable, buffer up to configured memory per-tenant and fall back to aggregated counters. Provide loss metrics to alerting.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Spike & prototyping (done): validated that OTLP metric attributes can be translated to Prom labels without losing cardinality invariants; microbenchmark for serialize/deserialize shows ~90us median in Rust implementation. (See spike notes below.)
2) Core RCA sidecar (MVP): sidecar receives lightweight JSON/otlp proto, enriches attributes (customer_alias -> canonical_customer, route -> route_id, model -> model_shard), enforces allowlists, emits OTLP+mTLS to telemetry gateway and a Prom remote_write compatible endpoint.
3) Sampling integration: expose HTTP control plane endpoint for dynamic sampling rules per-tenant; wiring to telemetry-orchestrator (ENG-314159).
4) Canary rollout: route 5% of requests from Hosted API through RCA with shadow dual-write, compare metrics with baseline for parity and perf.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Where to canonicalize customer identifiers vs. in downstream pipelines? RCA centralizes this for faster dashboard correctness but increases trust surface for PII handling. Raised for security review.
- Prom vs OTLP semantics: Prom label set explosion risk if we map every attribute; decision is to limit Prom labels to a small canonical set and send richer attributes via OTLP.
- Sidecar vs in-process SDK: sidecar simplifies rollout across languages but adds network hop; we will test both prototypes and consider in-process SDK for latency-critical paths later.

Acceptance criteria:
- RCA enriches >=95% of sampled requests with canonical context fields in staging and maintains <200us added p50 latency in edge canary.
- Prometheus dashboards show consistent per-route latency rollups (no duplicated high-cardinality labels) for canary traffic.
- OTLP attributes are consumed by KPI pipeline (telemetry-orchestrator) and correlate with traces in X% of samples (target 80%).
- Security review completed and approved for PII handling.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Request+Context+Assembler+RCA
- Spike microbench: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-spikes/pull/42
- Canary dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rca-canary/rca-canary-overview
- Telemetry orchestration workstream: ENG-314159

Spike notes:
- Prototype implemented in Rust (repo above). Benchmarks: 90us median, 220us p95 for enrich+emit to local NOP gateway.
- Verified OTLP attribute names: trace.attr.request_id, trace.attr.model_version, metric.attr.kv_cache_hit (boolean), metric.attr.prompt_bucket (low-cardinality).
- Memory model: per-tenant buffer capped at 25MB; eviction LRU by request_age.

Next steps:
- Finish sidecar feature parity for Prom remote_write and OTLP exporters (owner: Marco).
- Submit security review ticket with PII handling plan (owner: Aisha).
- Prepare canary plan and gating metrics for rollout (owner: Observability SRE).
